h4.title: The short-sentence standard stops at 1.5 s and the 完美 target ignores length: the teacher's own sub-1.5 s recordings mostly fail it
h4.scenario: A one-sentence paragraph or a subtitle cue (parse_script only merges sentences under 6 syllables within a paragraph; cues are never merged), for example 「好，下课。」, generated in 完美 or 极致.
h4.actual: g50_for uses np.interp over the points (1.5 s, 3.0 s, full). Below 1.5 s it clamps to the 1.5 s value, so very short sentences are still scored about 15 points low. effective_target() then requires pct >= natural p25, which is measured on full-length clips. Measured with the real models: the teacher's OWN held-out recordings pass the 完美 target only 16% of the time at 0.83 s of speech (median 82.9%) and 56% at 1.28 s, against 84-89% for 1.7 s and longer. Generation therefore cycles through extra batches (up to 20 tries; 12 on low tier) and keeps eliminating candidates as below 85%, chasing a level the teacher's own voice does not reach.
h4.evidence: speaker.py:802-805 `pts = sorted([... if float(k) < float(full)] + [(float(full), g50)]) ... return float(np.interp(float(seconds), xs, ys))`; SHORT_SECONDS = (1.5, 3.0) at line 523. engine.py:574-582 effective_target uses rng['p25'] with no length. t3_short_target.out: `redimnet2-b6 g50_for(0.8)= 11.358 g50_for(1.5)= 11.358 g50= 12.4352` and `2 words … 0.83s: median 82.9% pass 完美 target 16% pass 85% 47%`, `3 words … 1.28s: median 92.1% pass 完美 target 56%`.
h4.expected: For any length, the teacher's own recordings of that length average about 100%, and the 完美 target and the 85% filter are reachable by her own voice.
h4.fix: Add shorter crop lengths (for example 0.75 s and 1.0 s) to SHORT_SECONDS, or extrapolate below the first point, and bump CALIB_VERSION. Make effective_target length-aware (natural p25 per length bucket), or exempt short=True candidates from the pct part of _meets_targets/_pct_ok.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced the bug independently. I did not reuse the finder's speaker, and I also ran the real Narrator end to end. Scripts and outputs are in （临时目录）/hunt4/verify/eval_5/ (v1_short.py/.out, v2_engine.py/.out).

I ran them with /usr/bin/python3 because /tmp/gsv39 has no onnxruntime. In gsv39 the precise judge falls back to MFCC, sim_filter turns off, and this code path never runs. The real SV models came from the local scratchpad, so nothing was downloaded.

1) How it happens: speaker.py:523 sets `SHORT_SECONDS = (1.5, 3.0)`, and g50_for (speaker.py:802-805) uses np.interp, which clamps below the first point. Measured: g50_for(0.5) = g50_for(0.8) = g50_for(1.0) = g50_for(1.28) = g50_for(1.5) = 11.358, against g50 = 12.435 at full length. tests/test_sv.py:447 even pins g50_for(0.8)==g50_for(1.5). But the docstring says the whole point is that short sentences must not be "系统性地偏低十几个百分点", and below 1.5 s they still are.

2) The speaker's own held-out audio, scored by the real 3-model judge:
- English speaker 893705bb (完美 target 97.9): 0.77 s median 77.2%, 0% pass the target, 24% pass 85%. 1.12 s: 89.2%, 13% pass. 1.50 s: 99.0%, 55%. 3.0 s: 100%, 79%.
- English speaker 2aca1e72: 0.70 s 81.7% (0% pass the target); 0.95 s 90.2% (3%); 1.25 s 97.3% (52%).
- English speaker cce7416f: 0.99 s 94.7% (30%); 1.5 s 100% (80%).
- Chinese continuous speech, 4 speakers. I cropped validation clips that are not part of the average voiceprint. At 0.8 s the medians were 87.7 / 77.0 / 90.8 / 86.4%. At 1.0 s: 92.4 / 77.9 / 94.1 / 95.9%. At 1.5 s every speaker was at 99-100%.

3) End to end: the real Narrator in 完美 (tier high, 4 per batch, up to 20 tries, ASR off), with a "perfect clone" backend that returns the speaker's OWN held-out recordings.
- Two-word sentences, about 0.80 s of speech, 12 sentences: on average 15.3 of 20 tries, list [8,4,16,16,20,20,12,20,20,20,8,20]. Only 50% met the target. 6 of 12 ended ⚠️ with the hint 「这一句可能不够像，建议重新生成或改写」. SHORT_HINT does not appear, because the best candidate is ≥85%, so the teacher is told to regenerate or rewrite her own voice.
- Control, 8 words, about 2.96 s: always 4 tries, 100% met.

Why the teacher can reach it: parse_script (script.py:302-307) leaves a short sentence on its own when it is the only sentence in a paragraph. For example 「好，下课。」 (3 syllables) came out as its own segment in my test. Subtitle cues are never merged, and normal 6-7 syllable Chinese sentences run about 1.2-1.4 s of speech.

Why the existing safeguards do not cover it:
- effective_target (engine.py:574-582) uses natural p25 measured on full-length clips.
- _meets_targets (engine.py:567) and _pct_ok (engine.py:551) take no account of sentence length.
- The short-sentence mitigation (_is_short, below 2 s) only softens 🔴 to ⚠️. It does not change the target, the loop or the hint.

Not in research/全面找bug/README.md. The documented limitation (sv_benchmark 记录.md: 1.5 s scores 13 points low) is exactly what g50_short is meant to correct, and the correction stops at 1.5 s.

Real impact is limited:
- The chosen audio is still the best candidate, because the offset is the same for every candidate of that sentence.
- The harm is extra generation time per short sentence (about 4x tries), a percentage that reads 10-20 points low, and wrong "不够像，建议重新生成或改写" advice on some very short sentences.
verdict.fix:
Minimal fix, in voicetwin/eval/speaker.py:
- Line 523: change to `SHORT_SECONDS = (0.75, 1.0, 1.5, 3.0)`.
- Line 527: bump `CALIB_VERSION = 3`.

The calibration loop at lines 720-723 already crops any length (it needs speech ≥ 1.3× the crop) and keeps a median only when there are at least 3 values. So g50_for then interpolates down to 0.75 s and clamps only below that.

Recommended second part, in voicetwin/synth/engine.py:
- In _meets_targets (567-572) and _clearly_good, when the candidate has fewer than SHORT_WARN_SECONDS of speech (`_is_short(c.score)`), use self.min_pct instead of effective_target. Natural p25 comes from full-length clips, and short clips spread more widely, so even with correct centring her own short recordings would pass p25 only about 60% of the time.
- In the hint at lines 790-791, use SHORT_HINT instead of _target_miss for short sentences. This matches the existing policy that sentences under 2 s are never judged 不像.

What the fix could break or change:
- The CALIB_VERSION bump makes every voice recalibrate once on first use, a few extra embeddings per validation clip.
- It also changes judge.signature(), so every cached sentence has its pct rescored once (_rescore_cached; no audio is regenerated).
- Medians at 0.75 s are noisier when there are few validation clips.
- The second part lets some genuinely weaker short candidates count as met and stop after 4 tries. That is acceptable because scores at that length are unreliable anyway.
- tests/test_sv.py:441-449 uses its own {"1.5","3"} table and still passes. test_calibration_records_short_standards (line 494) still holds, and could be extended to assert short["0.75"] < short["1.5"].
- Nothing touches the title, the silence handling or the UI language.
verdict.notes:
The claim is substantially correct. The finder's numbers (0.83 s: median 82.9%, 16% pass) match what I measured on 3 other English speakers and 4 Chinese continuous-speech speakers.

One correction to the claim: in my runs even 1.5 s clips were not quite "fixed". At full length her own recordings pass the p25 target only about 64-94% of the time, which is expected because the target is p25. The clear defect is the monotone drop below 1.5 s.

The end-to-end run with real models confirms the consequence in the engine: about 4x the tries and a misleading hint for half of the very short sentences.

Severity stays low: no data loss, the best candidate is still chosen, and only time and wording are affected.

Environment notes:
- During the run the disk was nearly full because of other agents' files. I moved my workspace to /dev/shm and deleted it afterwards.
- Monitor's `kill -0` could not see my pids, which first made the runs look dead. I stopped the duplicate runs by pid.
- The repo is untouched (git status is clean).

h4.actual: build_profile stores quantiles() of English clip rates and pitch from as few as 1 clip. in_normal_range then demands rate within [p10*0.92, p90*1.08] and F0 within ±1 semitone of [p10, p90]. With 1 clip that is ±8% / ±1 semitone around that single clip. In a simulation where generated sentences come from exactly the teacher's own distribution (a perfect clone), only 11.8% (1 clip), 34.7% (2) and 49.8% (3) are 'in your normal range', against 82.9% with 30 clips. _meets_targets fails, so 完美 runs extra batches (up to 20 tries) and ends with 「这一句的语速或音调和你平时不太一样，建议重新生成或改写」, a claim based on one clip.

"f0_p10": np.percentile(meds, 10), "f0_p90": ...` (no minimum count). metrics.py:381-389 `lo, hi = rate_q["p10"] * ... * 0.92, rate_q["p90"] * ... * 1.08` / `pitch["f0_p10"] / 1.06 <= score.f0 <= pitch["f0_p90"] * 1.06`. engine.py:571 _meets_targets requires in_normal_range. t5_normal_range.out: `teacher has 1 English clips -> … 11.8%`, `2 … 34.7%`, `3 … 49.8%`, `30 … 82.9%`.

h4.title: Blind test says 「和瞎猜的 50% 差不多」 when listeners got 90% wrong
h4.scenario: Listeners consistently label the clean generated clips 真人 and the real recordings (which have room tone) 生成, so 18 of 20 answers are wrong. The teacher grades the answer sheet.
h4.actual: Any accuracy of 60% or less, including 0-20%, gets 「听众基本分辨不出（正确率 10%，和瞎猜的 50% 差不多）」 and no tips. 10% on 20 items is far below chance (p ≈ 0.0002): the listeners CAN tell the two apart, they just have the labels reversed.
h4.evidence: workflows.py:1285-1286 `elif acc <= 0.60: verdict = f"听众基本分辨不出（正确率 {acc:.0%}，和瞎猜的 50% 差不多）"`. t6_blind_verdict.out: `answered 20 correct 2 -> 听众基本分辨不出（正确率 10%，和瞎猜的 50% 差不多） []`.
h4.expected: Use a two-sided band around 50% (for example 40-60%). Well below chance gets a separate verdict, such as 「听众分得出来，但把生成的当成了真人（正确率 10%）」.
h4.fix: Add a branch for acc < 0.4 with honest wording; optionally show the binomial significance when the number answered is small.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced it. The code is at voicetwin/workflows.py:1283-1286: `elif acc <= 0.60: verdict = f"听众基本分辨不出（正确率 {acc:.0%}，和瞎猜的 50% 差不多）"`. It is a one-sided cut-off, so it has no lower bound. The web UI self-listen path has the same problem at voicetwin/webui/app.py:2422-2424 (`_blind_verdict`: `if acc <= 0.60: return "👍 听众基本分辨不出（和乱猜的 50% 差不多）。"`).

Repro script: （临时目录）/hunt4/verify/eval_8/repro.py. It builds a 20-item answer file in a temp dir and calls the real wf.grade_blind_test and app._blind_verdict. Output:
- correct 0/20, p=0.00000 -> 听众基本分辨不出（正确率 0%，和瞎猜的 50% 差不多）, tips=[]
- correct 2/20, p=0.00040 -> 听众基本分辨不出（正确率 10%，和瞎猜的 50% 差不多）, tips=[]
- correct 4/20, p=0.0118 -> 听众基本分辨不出（正确率 20%，和瞎猜的 50% 差不多）
- webui _blind_verdict(0.10) and (0.0) -> 👍 听众基本分辨不出（和乱猜的 50% 差不多）。

How the teacher reaches it: in ⑤ 鉴别, 「批改收上来的答题卡」 runs grade_blind_test and shows the verdict through _blind_grade_md. The in-page self-listen test goes through _blind_result_md -> _blind_verdict. The trigger is plausible. The real clips are denoised training material and may carry room tone or denoise artifacts, while the generated clips are digitally clean. A listener who goes by "clean = real" will mark the labels in reverse. A listener who mixes up which label means which also gets this result.

This is not intended design. The project rule is "不要乱写": text shown to the teacher must be true. Telling her 10% is "和瞎猜的 50% 差不多" is false, because 10% of 20 is very unlikely to be chance (two-sided p≈0.0004). It is not an accepted limitation, and it is not in research/全面找bug/README.md (no blind-test entries there).

Why it is low severity: you could argue the teacher's goal is still met, since listeners took the generated voice for real. Only the wording and the hidden signal are wrong. The hidden signal is that the two kinds of clips do sound different, for example the real recordings may have noise or denoise artifacts.
verdict.fix:
Make the same change in two places, both ahead of the existing `acc <= 0.60` branch:

1. voicetwin/workflows.py:1285, inside grade_blind_test: add a lower branch such as `elif acc < 0.40 and answered >= 10:` with honest wording, e.g. verdict = f"听众分得出两种声音，但大多把生成的当成了真人（正确率 {acc:.0%}，比瞎猜的 50% 还低很多）". Add one tip, e.g. "真实录音可能带底噪或降噪痕迹，听众反而觉得干净的生成音频更像真人；这说明生成的声音已经很像，但两种声音听起来确实不一样". Gating on answered >= 10 (or an exact two-sided binomial p < 0.05) is better than a bare 40% cut-off, so that small tests don't trigger it. For example, 1/4 = 25% is ordinary chance and should keep the current verdict plus the existing 「题目太少」 note.

2. voicetwin/webui/app.py:2422, `_blind_verdict(acc)`: add the same branch. It needs the answered count passed in from `_blind_result_md`, which already has `answered`. Alternatively add a plain `acc < 0.40` branch and keep the 「题目太少」 behaviour consistent.

What the fix could break:
- The existing tests only check acc=0.5 and 0.9 (tests/test_pipeline.py:659, tests/test_webui_helpers.py:545), so they still pass.
- The `_blind_verdict` signature changes, so check any other callers.
- Keep the wording in Chinese, written for the teacher, and keep the verdict free of invented numbers. Only the measured 正确率 is shown.
verdict.notes: The bug finder's claim is accurate, apart from a small p-value difference: they quoted p≈0.0002 (one-sided) and the two-sided value is ≈0.0004. Their repro at hunt4/eval/t6_blind_verdict.py gives the same output. The self-listen web UI path has the same text and was not mentioned in the claim. The fix should cover both places. Severity is low because the teacher's real goal (generated audio that passes as the teacher) is arguably met. The problem is a false statement plus a hidden signal, not broken output.

h4.title: 鉴别 says 「「综合 %」是它们的平均」, but 综合 is not the average of the per-model % shown
h4.scenario: The teacher scores files in ⑤ 鉴别 with the 3-model precise judge and checks the per-model numbers against 综合.
h4.actual: judge_embeddings caps each model's % at 0-100 for display, but 综合 = clamp(mean of the UNCAPPED values). With the real models, a failed sentence shows ReDimNet2 0.0 / ERes2NetV2 47.1 / ERes2Net-base 13.9 and 综合 14.8 (their average is 20.3). A good sentence with raw (108, 104, 96) shows 100 / 100 / 96 and 综合 100.0. The page still says the 综合 is their average.
h4.evidence: speaker.py:1021-1024 `pcts = {k: _clamp_pct(v) for k, v in raws.items()}; pct_raw = float(np.mean(list(raws.values()))) ... "pct": _clamp_pct(pct_raw)`. app.py:2302 `（几个模型分别打分，「综合 %」是它们的平均）`. t1 output (real ONNX models): `speech0.4s + silence 4s pct=14.8 raw=14.83 pcts={'redimnet2-b6': 0.0, 'eres2netv2-zh': 47.1, 'eres2net-base-zh': 13.9}`.
h4.expected: The explanatory text matches the computation; for example 「综合 % 按不封顶的分数平均后再限制在 0～100」, or show uncapped per-model values.
h4.fix: Change the UI sentence (or show per-model pct_raw) so the teacher can reproduce the 综合 number from what is displayed.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced this through the real path: SimilarityJudge.judge_file, then judge_embeddings, then webui/app.py `_verify_rows`, which renders the ⑤ 鉴别 table and summary. Script: （临时目录）/hunt4/verify/eval_9/repro.py, run with /tmp/gsv39/bin/python. It uses fake encoders with fixed embeddings, no network and no models.

Output:
- Case A (old one-sided calibration via p50, where raw can go above 100): pcts={'modelA': 100.0, 'modelB': 75.0}. The average of the displayed numbers is 87.5, but the 综合 cell shows '100.0%'.
- Case B (precise two-sided AS-norm, where raw can go below 0): pcts={'m1': 0.0, 'm2': 47.1, 'm3': 13.9}. The displayed average is 20.3, but 综合 shows '14.8%'.
- In both cases the summary line rendered is 「用到的声纹模型：…（几个模型分别打分，「综合 %」是它们的平均）」.

Cause: speaker.py:1021 caps each model's % on its own (`pcts = {k: _clamp_pct(v)...}`). Lines 1022/1024 average the uncapped raws and only then cap (`_clamp_pct(mean(raws))`). verify_files (workflows.py:1355-1369) passes both through as-is, and app.py:2302 states that 综合 is "their average".

Reachable: the teacher sees this in ⑤ 鉴别 whenever more than one model is loaded, which is the default precise 3-model ensemble. A single model above 100% is normal for good sentences, because natural_range p90 is above 100 by design, and a single model below 0% is normal for bad ones. So the mismatch will happen often in real use.

The 0/100 caps can also flip the ✅/🔴 the teacher would expect from the row. Example: raws 120 and 60 display as 100 and 60, which average 80, yet 综合 is 90 ✅.

It is not in research/全面找bug/README.md. The computation itself is intended: the judge_embeddings docstring says pct is the average then capped, and pct_raw is the uncapped average. Only the explanation shown to the teacher is wrong. The old docs/manual (07_ch10_12.html:263, «几个模型的平均») says the same thing, but CLAUDE.md says the long PDF manual is no longer maintained.

Not a scoring bug: ranking, pass/fail, and the 85% elimination are internally consistent. It is a misleading sentence, which goes against rule 7 (不要乱写) and rule 5 (explain clearly to the teacher).

Smallest correct fix: change only the sentence at voicetwin/webui/app.py:2302. For example: 「（几个模型分别打分；「综合 %」是几个模型原始分数的平均，再限制在 0%～100%。每个模型单独显示时最高只显示 100%、最低 0%，所以综合 % 不一定等于表里几个数字的平均）」. If docs/manual is ever rebuilt, update 07_ch10_12.html:263 the same way. No test asserts this text (grep of tests/ is empty), so the change breaks nothing.

Alternatives I do not recommend:
(a) Changing speaker.py:1022 to average the capped values. This changes `pct` everywhere it is used: the 85% auto-elimination in synth/engine.py:635, best-of-N selection in synth/select.py, metrics.py, and the signature/caching of previously scored sentences. It also loses the 'above 100' information the design keeps on purpose.
(b) Showing uncapped per-model values such as 125% or -16%. This breaks the 0～100 promise in PCT_HELP and could confuse the teacher more.

h5.title: The global stop flag leaks into the 校对表: saving a corrected grey row while a stopped task is still winding down raises TaskCancelled past _safe, half-applies the save and leaves 「保存修改」 / 「确认训练素材」 unresponsive until the page is reloaded
h5.scenario: A generation (or select / verify / blind test) runs in the background and the teacher clicks ⏹ 停止 twice. The task only stops at its next check: the current GPT-SoVITS request, scoring, then backend.stop() waiting up to 10 s. The 校对表 is not locked during these tasks. In those seconds she double-clicks a grey row (「没有识别出文字」, 「语速异常」, 「疑似识别错误」…), types the correct sentence, as the page suggests, and clicks 「保存修改」 or 「✅ 确认训练素材」.
h5.actual: save_rows writes the text and consumes the draft. apply_review → apply_filters then has to compute that row's voiceprint and calls _check_cancel(), which sees the process-wide CANCEL event and raises TaskCancelled, a BaseException. _safe and do_clip_action's `except Exception` do not catch it, and neither does gradio 4.24's queue (`except Exception`), so no process_completed message is ever sent: the click stays 'processing' forever (verified with gradio_client: status PROCESSING after 15 s). save_clips and confirm_btn use the default trigger_mode 'once'. The frontend only clears pending_request on 'data', so every later click on these buttons is ignored until a reload. On disk: text saved, but keep=False / drop_reason 「没有识别出文字」 (the row stays grey and not counted). The confirmation is not recorded. Clicking save again says 「没有需要保存的修改」 and does not re-run the statistics.
h5.expected: A stop request only affects the background task it was meant for. Table saves either finish normally or show a Chinese message.
h5.evidence: progress.py:57-72 `CANCEL = threading.Event()` (one flag for the whole process); check_cancel raises TaskCancelled(BaseException) (progress.py:50). prepare.py:400-403 `for j, r in enumerate(todo_emb): _check_cancel()` runs in apply_review (workflows.py:492-498) on the web handler thread. app.py:903-920 _safe: `except Exception`. app.py:3169 `except Exception as exc:  # noqa`. app.py:4443-4448: save_clips / confirm_btn click with no trigger_mode. gradio/queueing.py process_events only `except Exception` (no completion message for BaseException). Frontend Blocks-5950680d.js: `z.trigger_mode==="once"?z.pending_request||_e(W)`, and pending_request is reset only in the 'data' handler. Repro output (r1_stop_leak.py): `save RAISED past _safe: TaskCancelled 已按你的要求停止` / `after save: X text = 大家好… | keep = False | drop_reason = 没有识别出文字 | unsaved drafts = 0` / `confirm RAISED past _safe` / `confirmation recorded: False` / `save again: 没有需要保存的修改`. r1b_gradio_baseexc.py: `1st call (handler raised TaskCancelled): done=False after 15.0s, status=Status.PROCESSING`.
h5.fix: Make cancellation per task: store the task's thread id with request_cancel(), and have check_cancel() raise only in that thread (or in threads started by the task). Or pass a cancel token down instead of using the global Event. As a safety net, have _safe (and the try in do_clip_action) also catch TaskCancelled, so gradio always gets a reply.

verdict.evidence:
Code path confirmed. `progress.CANCEL` is a single `threading.Event` for the whole process. `request_stop()` sets it, and it is only cleared in the `finally` of the task thread (`tasks.py:264`). So it stays set from the moment the stop is confirmed until the task has wound down: the current engine request, the scoring, then `backend.stop()`. `apply_review` is only called from table handlers on the web thread (`review_save`/`confirm`/`delete`/`restore`) and from the CLI. Its `derive(snapshot)` runs `apply_filters`, and that function calls `_check_cancel()` for every newly active row that has no cached voiceprint (`prepare.py:401-402`). `TaskCancelled` is a `BaseException`, so it passes through `_safe` (`except Exception`, `app.py:909`) and through gradio 4.24 `queueing.process_events` (`except Exception` only). No `ProcessCompletedMessage` is sent. The frontend (`Blocks-5950680d.js`) only resets `pending_request` in the 'data' handler, so with the default `trigger_mode` 'once' every later click on that button is dropped. `_edit_guard` only covers prepare/proofcheck/textfix of the same voice. Generate, select, train, verify, blind and download do not lock the table.

Repro 1 (`verify/conflicts_2/v1_stop_window_save.py`): real `stream_task("generate", wf.run_narrate)` with the dummy engine taking 4 s per sentence, the real `WebUI.on_stop` clicked twice, the real `_safe(do_save)` and `_safe(do_confirm)`, and a grey row 「没有识别出文字」 edited as a draft. Output:
- `save RAISED past _safe after 0.02s: TaskCancelled 已按你的要求停止 | task still alive: True`
- `on disk: text='大家想一想，这段代码输出' keep=False drop_reason=没有识别出文字 unsaved drafts=0`
- `confirm RAISED past _safe`, `confirmation recorded: False`
- after the task ended: `save again: 没有需要保存的修改`, `row X still keep=False`
- a later confirm self-heals: `keep=True drop_reason=''`

Repro 2, real browser against the real app (`br_server.py` + `br_flow.py`, playwright chromium, gradio 4.24, dummy sentence = 10 s, `do_save`/`do_confirm` log a marker line). Steps: type the sentence into row X, click 生成 on ③, click ⏹ 停止 twice, go to ① and click 保存修改.
- 1.0 s after the stop, the server got `do_save` ("加载声纹模型…" then nothing, no reply). Row X on disk: text saved, keep False, drop_reason 没有识别出文字, drafts 0.
- Generation stopped 8.5 s after the stop.
- Clicks 2 and 3 on 保存修改 after that: `server calls + 0`. The browser drops them.
- ✅ 确认训练素材 (not clicked during the window) still works and repairs the row.
- After a page reload, 保存修改 works again.

1. The data damage is temporary. The next 「✅ 确认训练素材」, which training requires, re-runs `apply_review` and makes the row usable. Confirm is only stuck if it was also clicked inside the window.
2. It only fires when the saved change makes a row active that has no voiceprint yet: typing text into a grey 没有识别出文字 / 疑似识别错误 / 语速异常 row, as the page suggests. Saving ordinary rows never reaches `_check_cancel`.

The window is a few seconds to about 10-20 s after a stop, and the teacher has to switch tabs and click save inside it. Hence low severity.

A table recount is a short web-thread action and must never react to another task's stop. `run_prepare` (`prepare.py:599`) keeps the default, so stopping 准备素材 still works.

verdict.evidence:

The script starts tasks.stream_task("train", ...) with a fake training function that logs one line, waits on a gate, then raises "CUDA out of memory". While that runs, a separate thread (standing in for the gradio worker) does what the teacher would: it edits row 4 with ui.do_clip_action, then calls ui.do_save(VOICE). After that the gate is released.

The 问题报告 file has the same lines in its task-lines section (report lines 25-32).

Why it happens:
- tasks.py:238-240 adds a _LineHandler to the "voicetwin" logger.
- _LineHandler.emit (tasks.py:125-130) does no thread or voice filtering.
- _problem_report copies task.lines[-150:] (tasks.py:186-187).

Why the teacher can reach it: app.py:2865-2871 (_edit_guard) blocks 保存修改 only while prepare, proofcheck or textfix is running for the same voice. During training, 保存修改, 删除 and 恢复 all run (review_save, review_delete and review_restore call apply_review, which logs these lines). Table saves on a different voice also run during training, and their lines would land in voice A's training log too. I found nothing in 教学手册 or research/全面找bug/README.md that marks this as intended or already known, and no test covers it.

Two qualifications:
1. The report has a second section, the voicetwin.log tail since task.started (lines 43-66). Its file handler's _ProjectFilter lets through every thread bound to the same voice, so same-voice save lines will stay in that section even after a fix. verdict.fix:
Filter records in tasks.py: give _LineHandler a `filter` method (or check inside emit at tasks.py:125). Record the task thread's ident in _run (tasks.py:237, `threading.get_ident()`). Accept a record only if one of these holds:
- `record.thread == task_ident`
- `record.threadName.startswith("vt-")`, which covers the helper threads backends start inside the task: vt-poll-progress at backends/base.py:313, vt-cancel-watch at base.py:296 and vt-watch-download at utils/progress.py:867. Accepting these is safe because only one background task runs at a time.

h5.title: While a Stop is still in progress, 保存修改 / ✅ 确认训练素材 freeze for good, and the saved rows stay gray as 「没有识别出文字」
h5.scenario: A background task is running (generation, training, prepare, download or textfix of another voice). The teacher clicks ⏹ 停止 and confirms. The task needs a few seconds (sometimes tens of seconds, e.g. while a model loads or a sentence is being synthesized) to reach its next cancel check. During that time she types the text for a clip that has no text yet (双击「文字」, which the UI tells her to do for clips without text) and clicks 「保存修改」 or 「✅ 确认训练素材」.
h5.actual: CANCEL is one process-wide threading.Event, not tied to the task. review_save runs save_rows, which writes the texts and clears the drafts. It then calls apply_review → apply_filters, which runs _check_cancel() for every newly active clip whose voiceprint must be computed. That raises TaskCancelled, a BaseException. _safe(...) only catches Exception. gradio 4.24's process_events also only catches Exception, so the browser never gets a 'completed' message and the button spins forever. On disk, the rows now have text, are 🟢 saved, but keep keep=False and drop_reason=「没有识别出文字」 (not material). Clicking 保存 again just says there is nothing to save. Only a later 确认训练素材 re-derives the stats. The same applies to confirm (confirmation not recorded) and to 「💾 保存这一行」.
h5.expected: Stopping a background task should only affect that task. A table save running in another gradio thread should never see the stop flag.
h5.evidence: progress.py:57 `CANCEL = threading.Event()` (global); tasks.py:415 `request_cancel()`, cleared only at tasks.py:264 when the task thread ends. prepare.py:399-402 `todo_emb = [r for r in active if r["id"] not in cache]` / `for j, r in enumerate(todo_emb): _check_cancel()`. workflows.py:550 `res["summary"] = apply_review(cfg, voice, read_csv=False) if res["saved"] else None` (no re-derive on the next click because nothing is unsaved). app.py:911 `_safe` uses `except Exception`. app.py:4443/4446 wire do_save/do_confirm through _safe. Repro r1 output: `请求停止： True` / `❌ 保存被打断：TaskCancelled（BaseException）: 已按你的要求停止` / `这时还没保存的修改： 0` / `任务结束后再保存：saved 0`. Repro r1b output: 6 rows `text= True keep= False drop_reason= 没有识别出文字 is_material= False`, `material_counts ... 'material': 0`, `再点一次保存：saved 0 summary None`. Repro r1c (real gradio 4.24): `ok → '保存好了' (0.5 s)`, `exc → ValueError (0.1 s)`, `cancel → TimeoutError (15.0 s)`.
h5.fix: Make cancellation belong to the task. Store a threading.Event on _Task and expose it through a thread-local or contextvar set in _run, then have check_cancel() look only at the current thread's task event. Alternatively, make apply_filters (and other code reachable from synchronous handlers) skip cancel checks when not running in the task thread. Also catch BaseException (re-raising only SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt) in _safe, so a stray TaskCancelled can never leave a button spinning.

- `SAVE RAISED TaskCancelled through _safe after 0.04s`

It then calls apply_review → apply_filters, which reaches prepare.py:402 `_check_cancel()` for every newly active clip not yet in the embedding cache. TaskCancelled is a BaseException. _safe (app.py:911) and do_clip_action's handler (app.py:3169) only catch Exception.

Gradio 4.24 check (v2_gradio.py, a real server with gradio_client): `ok -> 'ok' 0.4s`, `cancel -> TimeoutError 10.0s`, `ok -> 'ok' 0.2s`. No completion message is ever sent. process_events' finally still frees the concurrency slot, so the queue does not deadlock. But save_clips and confirm_btn use the default trigger_mode="once" (blocks.py:985), so the browser ignores further clicks on those buttons until the page is reloaded. With show_progress="hidden", nothing on screen changes. The `.then(textfix_state)` step never runs.

Reachability: the stop window is short but real. Training notices the stop within about 1 s via the watcher, plus the time to kill the process tree on Windows. A download chunk can block up to its 60 s timeout. Prepare of another voice, and model or engine loads, can take tens of seconds. The save must also make a clip newly active that is not yet in the embedding cache. That happens when she types text for a clip with no text (the UI tells her to double-click 文字 for these), fixes a 「语速异常（文字可能不对）」 or 「疑似识别错误」 row, or restores a clip. A natural sequence is: type corrections while a task runs, stop it, then click 保存 or 确认 right away.

Not already fixed: nothing about it in research/全面找bug/README.md. It is not intended design and not an accepted limitation.

Why I rate it low rather than medium: nothing is lost (texts are saved). Training cannot use stale stats, because confirm is required and confirm re-derives. Reloading the page and clicking 确认 again fully recovers. And it needs a timing overlap of seconds.
verdict.fix:
Minimal, low-risk fix: make the synchronous web buttons ignore the global stop flag, and leave the task thread and its helper threads alone.

1. voicetwin/utils/progress.py, around lines 57-72: add a thread-local `_LOCAL = threading.local()` and a context manager `ignore_cancel()` that sets `_LOCAL.ignore = True` for the duration and restores the old value in finally. Change check_cancel to `if CANCEL.is_set() and not getattr(_LOCAL, 'ignore', False): raise TaskCancelled(...)`. Expose a matching helper, for example `cancel_active()`, and use it in voicetwin/backends/base.py cancel_requested() (line 85), which reads _CANCEL directly. The watcher thread at base.py:290 can keep reading CANCEL as it does now, because it only runs inside tasks.

2. voicetwin/webui/app.py:907-911 (_safe wrapper): run `fn` inside `with ignore_cancel():`. As a fallback, add `except TaskCancelled as exc:` that returns a friendly Markdown message, so a stray cancel can never leave a button stuck pending.

This covers 保存修改, 确认训练素材 and the table's save_row, delete and restore, because clip_action_btn is wrapped in _safe too.

What it could break: any _safe-wrapped handler that was meant to be interruptible by ⏹ 停止. There is none today: request_stop only acts on a stream_task thread, and _safe handlers never run in one. Tests that call check_cancel directly on the main thread are unaffected, because the flag is thread-local and only set inside _safe. Streaming handlers that use stream_task keep the current behaviour.

A more thorough alternative is a threading.Event per _Task, published through a thread-local or contextvar set in tasks._run. It is more invasive and risks missing helper threads, such as thread pools and the base.py cancel watcher, that call check_cancel from threads _run did not set up, which could silently break ⏹ 停止.

- 72 clips give 9 val. Adding 8 clips makes need=1, prepare gives 11 against a target of 10, and the next save/confirm gives 10.
- 81 clips give 10 val. The teacher deletes one 考试题 (80 kept, target still 10, need=1) and the count goes UP to 11. The next save/confirm brings it back to 10.

Cause: prepare.py:462 `share = max(2 if len(items) >= 10 else 0, round(need*len(items)/total))` is applied per language with nothing capping the total at `need`, and rounding across languages can also overshoot. The next assign_splits call then reaches prepare.py:449-451 and trims `current[count:]` in manifest order.

Reachable paths:
- prepare: workflows.run_prepare -> prepare.py:600
- every save, delete, restore and confirm: workflows.apply_review -> derive -> workflows.py:537

Why the impact is low:
- Training requires confirm, and confirm runs apply_review first. So training always uses the trimmed count, and the training log matches the confirmation counts.
- material_signature has no split field, so confirmation is not invalidated.
- What the teacher sees: 「其中 X 条训练、Y 条当「考试题」」 changes (12 -> 10, or 10 -> 11 -> 10 after a delete) with no action from her. Per-language balance of the 考试题 shifts. select_references picks only from train clips, so the reference pool can change too.

Checks:
- Not listed in research/全面找bug/README.md.
- Not one of the intended designs or accepted limitations.
verdict.fix:
Change voicetwin/data/prepare.py assign_splits, lines 457-468, so the clips newly marked val never total more than `need`:
- Count each language's existing val clips toward its minimum of 2, using `max(0, 2 - existing_val_in_lang)` when len(items) >= 10.
- Then cap the shares. If sum(shares) > need, take the excess off the languages with the largest share, never going below the minimum still missing. If the minimums alone are more than need, accept that small overshoot only in that case, or give the minimums priority within need.
- Alternative: after the loop, un-mark extra newly picked clips (never ones already val) until the val total equals count.

Optional: when picking new val clips, prefer clips from sources that are not yet trained, or at least not the current train clips. When trimming in the `need <= 0` branch, drop newly added val clips before long-standing ones rather than going by id order.

What it could break:
- A language could get fewer than 2 new 考试题 when need is small. Speaker-eval calibration that wants at least 2 English val clips could see one fewer (eval/speaker.py:643 and 914 use the val split). Counting existing per-language val toward the minimum avoids this.
- Existing voices already over target are trimmed once on their next apply_review, which is what happens now.
- Tests only assert val_clips >= 1 (tests/test_pipeline.py:18), so they are not affected.
- Which clips are val changes slightly for future batches, so the reference picks (train-only pool) can differ.
verdict.notes: I could not refute the main claim. One part I did not verify: whether old-trained clips becoming 考试题 actually hurts model selection. That depends on whether a new training run starts from the base model (then it is harmless) or compares against the old model on these val clips. It also happens even with an exact count, because the pool includes every kept non-val clip, so it is a separate design point, not part of this count bug. The finder's e2e figure (confirm val=9) also includes an unsaved draft edit in s7_batch2.py. My clean run with no edits shows 12 -> 10, and the bug stands either way.

4. AFTER:

h6.title: The v18.5 fix for an old version still running is incomplete: two launcher paths open the OLD version's page with no version check
h6.scenario: The teacher upgrades to v18.5 (or later) while the old black window is still open, for example during training, so the laptop is busy. She double-clicks the desktop icon. At that moment the old process answers /config slowly once (more than the 2 s timeout). Every version since v0.1.6 holds the instance lock voicetwin_webui_7860.lock for its whole life, so the new launcher misses the old instance in its first scan, cannot get the lock and takes the 'starting elsewhere' path. One second later it finds the old instance and opens it. The same thing happens if the single miss lands inside the wait-for-old-to-close loop.
h6.expected: The new launcher keeps saying that the old version is still open. It opens the page only if the running instance is the same version, and it starts the new version only after the old process has really exited (for example, once the instance lock can be acquired).
h6.actual: Variant 1 prints 「声音分身正在另一个黑色窗口里启动（刚才可能连着双击了两次图标）」, then 「声音分身已经在运行了……已经帮你打开网页。这个窗口可以关掉。」, and opens the v18.4 page. Variant 2 prints 「旧版本已经关掉了，正在启动新版本……」 although the old version is still running, then opens the old page in the same way. The new version never starts, and the teacher sees the old interface with no new features. This is exactly the problem v18.5 claimed to fix (「新版本直接打开旧网页（标题都是 v18，分不出来），老师以为升级失败」). The port-error path at :358-361 has the same missing check.
h6.evidence:
launcher.py:311-326: only the first `_find_existing` hit gets `_instance_version` compared. The wait loop `while _find_existing(host, port):` (:322) exits on one missed 2 s request (`_existing_instance(..., timeout=2.0)` at :98-107 returns False on any exception). launcher.py:329-337: `lock = _acquire_instance_lock(port)`; `if lock is None: ... existing = _wait_for_existing(host, [port], 1.0)`; `if existing: _open_existing(existing, local); return` (no version check). :358-360: same `_wait_for_existing` → `_open_existing` with no version check. Every launcher since 610c474 (v0.1.6) has `_acquire_instance_lock`, so an old window always holds the lock.
Repro output (fake old v18.4 server whose first /config takes 2.5 s; the lock is held like a real old window):
声音分身正在另一个黑色窗口里启动（刚才可能连着双击了两次图标）。…
声音分身已经在运行了（在另一个黑色窗口里），已经帮你打开网页。这个窗口可以关掉。
browser opened: ['http://127.0.0.1:53239']
running old version is 18.4, this launcher is 18.5
Variant (third request slow): 「…旧版本的声音分身（v18.4）…」 → 「旧版本已经关掉了，正在启动新版本……」 → 「…已经帮你打开网页…」, browser opened the old URL.
h6.fix: Route every `_open_existing` call through the version check (wait-for-existing results and the OSError path too); on a mismatch, go to the old-version wait. In the old-version wait, do not leave the loop after one `_find_existing` miss: require `_acquire_instance_lock(port)` to succeed, since the old process releases it only when it exits, or require several misses in a row. Treat an `_instance_version` read failure as unknown and retry, not as an old version. Separately, OLD_RUNNING_MSG calls any different running version 「旧版本」, even a newer one (for example when an older second install is started).

verdict.evidence:
Code (current HEAD e02dd2f, voicetwin/webui/launcher.py):
- :311-326: the version check `_instance_version(existing) == __version__` runs only after the first `_find_existing` hit. The old-version wait `while _find_existing(host, port):` (:322) stops after ONE miss. `_existing_instance` (:98-107) returns False on any exception, including the 2 s timeout.
- :329-337 (STARTING_ELSEWHERE loop) and :358-361 (OSError path): `_wait_for_existing` -> `_open_existing` with no version check.
- An old window always holds `voicetwin_webui_<port>.lock` for its whole life. I checked v18.4 (d2483ac): `_acquire_instance_lock` comes before `app.launch`, which blocks, and the lock is released only in `finally`. It has existed since 610c474 (v0.1.6). So once the new launcher misses the old instance, it cannot get the lock and falls into the path with no version check.

My own end-to-end repro uses the real gradio 4.24 app as the OLD window, started through the real `launcher.launch` with `__version__` patched to 18.4, so it holds the real lock. The new launcher is unmodified v18.5 logic; only `_build` and `webbrowser.open` are stubbed. The only artificial element is one 2.5 s SIGSTOP stall of the old process. Scripts are in （临时目录）/hunt4/verify/windows_1/ (old.py, new.py, drive.py, drive_race.py).
- Control, no stall: prints 「另一个黑色窗口里还开着旧版本的声音分身（v18.4）…」 and keeps waiting (correct).
- Variant 1, stall during the first scan: call #1 -> None -> 「声音分身正在另一个黑色窗口里启动…」 -> call #2 finds the old instance -> 「声音分身已经在运行了…已经帮你打开网页」. Browser opened http://127.0.0.1:7957, which is still the v18.4 instance.
- Variant 2, a single stall while waiting for the teacher to close the old window: 「旧版本…（v18.4）…」 -> call #3 -> None -> 「旧版本已经关掉了，正在启动新版本……」 (false; the old process is still alive) -> 「…正在另一个黑色窗口里启动…」 -> 「…已经帮你打开网页」. The old v18.4 page opened and the new version never started.
- Variant 3, no stall: the old window is still building its page (lock held, port not open) when the new launcher starts. The new launcher goes straight to STARTING_ELSEWHERE and opens the old page. This one is deterministic, but it needs old and new started within about 30 s of each other, i.e. two installs.

How likely: the real /config is 231 KB and answers in 3 ms (measured 5 times), so variants 1 and 2 need a stall of more than 2 s, which is about 700 times normal. Training runs in a subprocess, so the webui process itself is idle. A plausible cause on Windows is a busy laptop that trimmed or paged out the idle old process, so the first request is cold and the next is warm. That matches variant 1 exactly. Variant 2 gets a fresh chance every ~2 s for up to 30 min. The condition the fix targets (upgrading while the old window is open) is the scenario v18.5 itself names, and the installer's Wait-OldClosed can be skipped with Y. Not intended design. Not listed as fixed or accepted in research/全面找bug/README.md (row 102 describes only the first-scan fix).

Severity is low, not medium: it needs a rare timing event; it is recoverable (close all windows, double-click again); no data is lost; the new version is installed, just not started.
verdict.fix:
voicetwin/webui/launcher.py, launch():
1. Move the version decision into one helper, e.g. `_handle_existing(existing, host, port, local) -> bool` ("handled, return"). It opens the page only when `_instance_version(existing) == __version__`. Otherwise it runs the old-version wait. Call it at all three places: the first scan (:311), the STARTING_ELSEWHERE loop (:333-335), and the OSError path (:358-360).
2. Old-version wait (:321-326): do not leave the loop after one `_find_existing` miss. Leave only when `_acquire_instance_lock(port)` returns an fd, since an old window releases the lock only when its process exits. Keep that fd as `lock` and skip the second acquire. If the lock comes back as -1 (lock file can't be created), fall back to requiring about 3 misses in a row, with the port bindable.
3. `_instance_version` (:110-123): return None on a read failure, kept separate from "" (a page without the vt-version marker). Retry 2-3 times before treating the instance as another version. Otherwise one slow read makes a same-version double-click say 「旧版本还开着」 and asks the teacher to close a working window.
Optional: OLD_RUNNING_MSG says 「旧版本」 even when the running version is newer.
What it could break:
- tests/test_launcher.py fakes that simulate "old closed" by making `_find_existing` return None without releasing a lock. With a lock-based exit they still pass if the fake old instance never took the lock; a fake that holds the lock must release it.
- A same-version double-click during startup now makes one extra /config request.
- If a second NEW launcher (double-click) grabs the lock first, the old-version wait must re-check `_find_existing` and the version, so it doesn't wait forever on its own sibling.
verdict.notes: All three variants reproduce against the real gradio app with the real file lock. The only artificial part is the stall (SIGSTOP), or the simultaneous start in variant 3. How often the teacher would hit it depends on a stall of more than 2 s, which I could not produce naturally (normal /config latency is 3 ms). That is why I rated it low, not the claimed medium. Every test process I started has exited, confirmed through pid files.

h6.title: GPU badge shows a green 「✅ 显卡正常」 when the bundle's PyTorch cannot load (WinError 1455 / 126); training uses that same PyTorch
h6.scenario: The teacher's 8 GB laptop has a small page file. `import torch` in the GPT-SoVITS bundle then fails with OSError [WinError 1455] 页面文件太小, which the GPT-SoVITS FAQ lists as a common problem; a missing DLL gives WinError 126 the same way. The web page's GPU badge is the main 'is my computer OK' indicator the quick start tells her to look at.
h6.expected: In the bundle runtime, a PyTorch import error other than ImportError (DLL load failure, page file) should show red or yellow and point to the existing 「电脑的虚拟内存不够」 advice (errors.py:411 already has that rule), because training will fail with the same error.
h6.actual: `_load_torch` returns (None, 'OSError…'), so `_probe` takes the 'no PyTorch / CPU PyTorch' branch, trusts nvidia-smi and reports level ok, 「✅ 显卡正常：NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU（显存 8.0 GB，可用 6.7 GB）」, with tier 'mid'. The error appears only in the hover tooltip.
h6.evidence:
gpu.py:160-161 `except Exception as exc: # OSError: [WinError 126] 等 return None, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"[:300]`; gpu.py:368-375: no torch → `_set_working(st, g["name"], …)` (level ok). Repro output: level: ok | message: ✅ 显卡正常：NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU（显存 8.0 GB，可用 6.7 GB） | torch_cuda: None tier: mid
✅ 显卡正常…
h6.fix: When torch_err is non-empty (import raised something other than ImportError), set level error or warn with a reason such as 「训练程序（PyTorch）打不开」, and use the errors.py pagefile or DLL advice instead of the nvidia-smi-only green result.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced this with the real code path and nothing patched. The finder's repro stubbed _load_torch; mine does not. Script: （临时目录）/hunt4/verify/windows_2/repro.py. It puts a fake `torch` package first on sys.path whose __init__ raises OSError("[WinError 1455] 页面文件太小… Error loading …cudnn_cnn64_9.dll"), which is how torch/__init__.py fails on Windows when it loads its DLLs. It also puts a fake executable `nvidia-smi` on PATH, so _find_nvidia_smi and _run_nvidia_smi run for real. Run with /tmp/gsv39/bin/python. Output:
- `_load_torch -> (None, 'OSError: … [WinError 1455] 页面文件太小…')`
- `level: ok | ok: True | source: nvidia-smi | torch_cuda: None`
- `message: ✅ 显卡正常：NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU（显存 8.0 GB，可用 6.7 GB）`, advice ''
- `tier: mid`
- The badge is `<div class="vt-gpu vt-gpu-ok" …>`. The error appears only in its title tooltip.
- Doctor NVIDIA row: (True, '✅ 显卡正常…'). The doctor's PyTorch row shows only ⚠️ with the raw English/OSError text.
- When training hits the same text, errors.explain turns it into 「电脑的虚拟内存不够」 with the pagefile advice.

Why it is reachable: option 1, the recommended install_windows.ps1 mode (`-Mode gsv`, install_windows.ps1:347-360), runs the web UI in GPT-SoVITS\runtime\python.exe. That is the same interpreter and the same torch that training and api_v2 use. So when `import torch` fails there, training and generation will fail too, while the main 'is my computer OK' badge stays green. The code already knows this distinction: workflows.py:1526 detects `in_gsv_runtime` for its own PyTorch row. gpu._probe (gpu.py:385-391) does not; it treats every import error as 'no torch'.

Is it intended? Partly. tests/test_gpu.py:223-227 deliberately asserts level=='ok' for a WinError 126 import failure. That choice is right for the .venv mode, where the web process's CPU torch is not the training torch. Nothing considers the gsv-runtime case, and research/全面找bug/README.md does not list it as an accepted limitation. Triggering it needs `import torch` to raise a non-ImportError in the web process: WinError 1455 on a small page file or 8 GB RAM, or WinError 126 when a DLL is missing or quarantined. Both are known GPT-SoVITS-on-Windows failures. They are uncommon in a single process, though; 1455 shows up more often in multi-process training.

Why severity is low: the GPU itself really is fine. The environment check shows a ⚠️ PyTorch row (raw text). When training fails, the teacher gets correct Chinese advice through errors.py:411 or :527. The harm is a false 'all clear' up front, plus tier 'mid', which recommends 完美 quality.
verdict.fix:
Change voicetwin/utils/gpu.py `_probe`, in the 'no PyTorch / CPU PyTorch' branch (gpu.py:385-391), plus a small helper:
1. Add `_in_gsv_runtime()`, the same check as workflows.py:1526: `(Path(sys.executable).resolve().parent.parent / 'api_v2.py').exists()`, wrapped in try/except so it returns False on error.
2. When `torch is None and torch_err and _in_gsv_runtime()` and nvidia-smi reports the card as fine, build the working result as now and then override it. Use level='warn' and keep ok=True so vram_tier keeps the real tier. Message: 「⚠️ 显卡正常，但训练程序（PyTorch）打不开」. For the advice, use errors.explain(torch_err), imported lazily inside try/except. That gives 「电脑的虚拟内存不够…调大虚拟内存」 for 1455, and the DLL / reinstall advice for 126. If explain fails, fall back to 「请重新双击 install_windows.bat 安装一次」. Keep torch_err in detail.
3. Add a test next to test_broken_torch_import_falls_back_to_nvidia_smi that monkeypatches the runtime check to True and expects warn. Keep the existing test, which covers the .venv mode, as ok.

What it could break:
(a) If the runtime detection is wrong, .venv users would see a false yellow badge. That is why the fix gates on the api_v2.py check rather than on torch_err alone.
(b) Choosing level='error' instead would make vram_tier return 'none'. That flips the recommended quality to 均衡. It also makes GPTSoVITSBackend._gpu_memory skip the badge and fall back to gpu_memory_gb, a subprocess import that would also fail and return 0, which brings up the CPU-training warning. Hence warn.
(c) The doctor's 'NVIDIA 显卡' row (workflows._gpu_row) would turn ⚠️ and partly repeat the PyTorch row. That is acceptable.
(d) WinError 1455 can be transient. The 10-second cache re-imports torch on refresh, so the badge can return to green on its own, which is fine.
verdict.notes: The finder's repro replaced _load_torch with a lambda. I confirmed that the real except branch (gpu.py:160-161) produces the same tuple when an actual `import torch` raises OSError, and that the real nvidia-smi subprocess path then yields the green badge. The finder's claim that 'training uses that same PyTorch' holds only for the recommended gsv-runtime install. In .venv mode the current green result is correct, and that is why tests/test_gpu.py asserts it. Doctor (workflows.py:1534-1535) does surface the import error as a ⚠️ 'PyTorch 显卡加速' row, but it shows raw OSError text, not the Chinese pagefile advice. I made no repo edits; all files are under the verify/windows_2 scratchpad.

install_windows.ps1:126-131 (Resolve-GsvRoot):

- If there are several:
  1. Return the one equal to the remembered root. Get it with `$rem = Get-RememberedGsv` and compare with -ieq after `[IO.Path]::GetFullPath(...).TrimEnd('\','/')` on both sides, because config.yaml stores forward slashes.

h6.title: Installer is silent for about 15 s on every run while it checks ports 7860-7869; a busy old instance is treated as closed
h6.scenario: Any install or upgrade on Windows. Right after 「安装位置：…」, Wait-OldClosed calls Test-VoiceTwinRunning, which makes an HTTP request to each of the 10 ports with a 1.5 s timeout. On Windows, connecting to a closed local port takes about 2 s to fail (handbook 十九: 「连接已关闭的本机端口要等约 2 秒才失败」), so each closed port costs the full 1.5 s.
h6.expected: A quick check (bind or TCP probe with a short timeout, as launcher._find_existing does), or at least a line like 「正在检查声音分身是不是还开着……」 before it.
h6.actual: About 15 s with no output at the very start of the installer, and the same again after each Enter in the wait loop. A teacher may think the window has frozen and close it. In the other direction, an old instance busy for more than 1.5 s (training) is reported as not running, and the install continues under it. This is the installer half of the v18.5 fix (「安装程序开始前也检查、请老师先关掉」).
h6.evidence: install_windows.ps1:303-313 `foreach ($port in 7860..7869) { … $req.Timeout = 1500; $resp = $req.GetResponse() … } catch {}`; :318 `if (-not (Test-VoiceTwinRunning)) { return }` (nothing printed before it); :324 rechecks all 10 ports after every Enter.
h6.fix: First skip ports where nothing is listening, using a 200 ms TcpClient ConnectAsync wait or an exclusive bind test, and only send HTTP to ports that are listening. Print a one-line Chinese status before scanning.

verdict.evidence:
The main claim holds: the installer goes quiet for about 15 s. The second half (a busy instance treated as closed) did not hold up in practice.

Code path (current HEAD e02dd2f):
- install_windows.ps1:342 calls `Wait-OldClosed` on every run, right after 「安装位置：…」 / Show-ExistingVoices / Check-OtherInstall and before the 「请选择安装方式」 menu.
- :318 `if (-not (Test-VoiceTwinRunning)) { return }` runs with no message printed first.
- :303-313 sends a plain HTTP GET to http://127.0.0.1:7860..7869/config, one port after another, with `$req.Timeout = 1500`. It only stops early when it finds an instance.
- install_windows.bat:20 runs it with Windows PowerShell 5.1 (`powershell`, so .NET Framework HttpWebRequest). There, Timeout bounds the whole GetResponse, connect included.
- The project itself records that on Windows, connecting to a closed local port takes about 2 s to fail: 教学手册.md:729 and research/时间线.md:243 (「检查推理服务是否就绪时 Windows 上每次卡 2 秒 → 先用 0.5 秒检查本机端口」, measured on Windows CI).
- The launcher already avoids this. launcher._find_existing (launcher.py:172-183) does a bind test first and only tries a 0.3 s connect on the preferred port, with the comment 「Windows 上连接关闭的端口比较慢」. The installer half of the v18.5 fix (research/全面找bug/README.md:102) never got this treatment.
- So in the common case, when no old copy is open (fresh install, or the teacher already closed it), the window stays silent for 10 x min(1.5 s, ~2 s), about 15 s. In the wait loop, :324 rescans all 10 ports after the teacher closes the old window and presses Enter, so there is another ~15 s of silence before 「好的，已经关掉了」.

Reproduction: （临时目录）/hunt4/verify/windows_4/repro.py, output in result.txt.
- There is no pwsh on this machine, so the script copies Test-VoiceTwinRunning line for line into Python (proxy off, 1.5 s timeout, same port loop).
- It runs inside `unshare -n`, a private network namespace, so nothing else on the machine is affected. iptables drops the SYN for closed ports. That stands in for the Windows slow refusal; the real Windows TCP stack was not run.
- Results:
  - A) nothing running: result=False after 15.0 s of silence.
  - B) old instance on 7860: found in 0.00 s.
  - C) instance whose /config takes 2 s: reported as NOT running, after 15.0 s.
  - D) launcher._find_existing under the same conditions: 0.30 s.

The "busy instance treated as closed" half is real in code (scenario C) but unlikely to happen. In gradio 4.24, /config is a sync route (routes.py:398) served from the threadpool. Training runs GPT-SoVITS as a subprocess, so /config normally answers quickly even while training. The launcher's own probe uses a similar 2 s timeout. I treat that half as speculative.

Severity is low. The installer still works; it only looks frozen at the very start, for a teacher who is not used to computers, and they might close the window.
verdict.fix:
The fix goes in install_windows.ps1:301-318.
(1) In Wait-OldClosed, print a status line before the first check, e.g. `Write-Host "正在检查声音分身是不是还开着（几秒钟）……"`.
(2) In Test-VoiceTwinRunning, find out which ports are actually listening before sending any HTTP:
`$listen = @(); try { $listen = @([System.Net.NetworkInformation.IPGlobalProperties]::GetIPGlobalProperties().GetActiveTcpListeners() | ForEach-Object { $_.Port }) } catch { $listen = 7860..7869 }`
then `foreach ($port in 7860..7869) { if ($listen -notcontains $port) { continue } ... }`.
This lookup is instant and opens no connections. Another option is a TcpClient.BeginConnect plus WaitOne(300) check before each HTTP request.
Because only listening ports get the HTTP request now, its timeout can safely go up to about 3000 ms. That also covers the rare slow /config response.

What it could break:
- GetActiveTcpListeners can throw on locked-down machines. The try/catch above falls back to the old full scan.
- A port bound to a single LAN address would still show as listening, but the HTTP request to 127.0.0.1 would fail just as it does today.
- The file must stay UTF-8 with BOM and CRLF (handbook 十九). tests/test_installers.py:202 asserts "Check-OtherInstall\r\nWait-OldClosed\r\n", so keep those two call lines unchanged and put the new message inside the function.
verdict.notes: The Windows TCP behaviour was emulated (SYN dropped inside a private netns), not run on Windows; the ~2 s refusal comes from the project's own Windows CI note. One side effect seen in the first repro run: scenario D took 2.0 s only because port 7860 was still in TIME_WAIT from the test server in scenario C. In a fresh namespace it took 0.30 s, so this is not a launcher problem.

h6.title: install.sh --gsv regenerates config.yaml with --force on every reinstall or upgrade (settings reset; voices seem to disappear if workspace was changed)
h6.scenario: A Linux/macOS user who installed with `bash install.sh --gsv /path/GPT-SoVITS` and later set workspace (or other settings) in config.yaml runs the same command again to upgrade.
h6.expected: Keep the existing config.yaml and only update backends.gptsovits.root and backend, as the Windows installer does (init-config without --force calls update_config_file).
h6.actual: `init-config … --force` overwrites config.yaml with the defaults (old copy saved as config.yaml.bak). workspace goes back to ./workspace, so the program shows no voices, and every tuned setting is lost.
h6.evidence: install.sh:43 `"$PY" -m voicetwin init-config --gptsovits-root "$GSV" --backend gptsovits --force`; cli.py:465-488: without --force an existing config is only updated ("其余设置保持不变"); with --force `write_example_config(path, repl, overwrite=True)` replaces it. The venv branch (:55) correctly does `[[ -f config.yaml ]] || init-config`.
h6.fix: Drop --force (init-config already updates root and backend in place when the file exists).

verdict.evidence:
The code does what the claim says. The line is actually install.sh:42 (the claim says 43): `"$PY" -m voicetwin init-config --gptsovits-root "$GSV" --backend gptsovits --force`. In cli.py main() (around lines 465-488), an existing config.yaml without --force goes through update_config_file, which changes only the keys passed and prints "其余设置保持不变". With --force it calls write_example_config(path, repl, overwrite=True). config.py:165-174 then copies the old file to config.yaml.bak (config.py:159-162, shutil.copy2) and writes the default template with only root and backend filled in. The venv branch (install.sh:53) correctly uses `[[ -f config.yaml ]] || init-config`, and install_windows.ps1:426-429 calls init-config without --force.

Reproduced with （临时目录）/hunt4/verify/windows_5/repro.sh (/tmp/gsv39/bin/python, temp dir, no network). It creates a config, sets `workspace: /data/my_voices`, then runs the exact install.sh:42 command:
- First rerun: config.yaml has `workspace: ./workspace` again; the .bak still has /data/my_voices.
- Second rerun (a second upgrade): config.yaml and config.yaml.bak both say `./workspace`. The user's settings are gone for good, because _backup copies the defaults over the only backup.
- Without --force: the output is "已更新 …：backends.gptsovits.root = …/GSV2，backend = gptsovits（其余设置保持不变）" and workspace stays /data/my_voices.

Why the teacher cannot reach it: 教学手册.md says she uses a Windows 11 laptop and installs from the Releases zip with install_windows.bat. scripts/build_windows_release.py:26 lists INCLUDE = ["voicetwin", "docs", "install_windows.bat", "install_windows.ps1", "pyproject.toml", "README.md"], so install.sh is not even in her package. The Windows installer already keeps her existing config. Only Linux/macOS users of the public repo who rerun `bash install.sh --gsv …` are affected. This is not intended design, not an accepted limitation, and not listed in research/全面找bug (that folder mentions install.sh only for the pypinyin/jieba extras issue).
verdict.fix:
install.sh:42: remove `--force`, so the line is `"$PY" -m voicetwin init-config --gptsovits-root "$GSV" --backend gptsovits`. On a first install, config.yaml does not exist yet and write_example_config(overwrite=False) creates it exactly as before. On a rerun or upgrade, init-config uses update_config_file and changes only backends.gptsovits.root and backend. It saves a .bak only when something actually changes, and keeps every other setting and comment.

Possible side effects:
- A very old or hand-trimmed config.yaml that lacks one of those keys now gets a printed warning ("…没有 … 这一项，已跳过") and that key is not set. Before, the file was silently rebuilt.
- A user who relied on the rerun to pick up new template sections or comments no longer gets them. Missing keys still fall back to the defaults when the config loads, so this costs nothing in practice.
- The exit code is still 0, so `set -e` does not stop the script. Nothing changes on Windows.
verdict.notes: This is a real, reproduced data-loss bug in the Linux/macOS installer. It is a bit worse than claimed: a second rerun also overwrites config.yaml.bak with the defaults, so the original settings cannot be recovered at all. It is still low severity because the teacher (Windows only) can never hit it; install.sh is not shipped in the Windows release zip.
